blurb: Small white Japanese spitz with a stand-off coat that sheds dirt easily
description: The Japanese Spitz is a small companion spitz from Japan with a thick pure-white double coat, prick ears and a curled plumed tail; lively and loyal.
answer: The Japanese Spitz is a small to medium spitz-type companion dog developed in Japan in the 1920s and 1930s. It typically stands about 30 to 38 cm tall, has a thick pure-white double coat, and is commonly described as active, loyal and affectionate.

body: Japanese breeders created the Japanese Spitz in the 1920s and 1930s by crossing several spitz breeds, starting with white German Spitz dogs that had come to Japan from northeastern China and were first shown in Tokyo in 1921. Between 1925 and 1936 small white spitz dogs from around the world were added. The final standard was written after World War II and accepted by the Japan Kennel Club.

The breed became popular in Japan in the 1950s and was exported to Sweden and then England, where the Kennel Club recognised it in 1977. It is now recognised by most major kennel clubs; the American Kennel Club added it to its Foundation Stock Service in 2019.

The Japanese Spitz has a somewhat square body, a deep chest, a wedge-shaped face with a pointed muzzle and small triangular prick ears. Its thick, pure-white double coat has an outer coat that stands off from a soft undercoat, with a ruff around the neck and a long, heavily furred tail curled over the back. The black nose, lips, eye rims and pads contrast with the white coat. It is always larger than the Pomeranian, though ideal sizes vary between kennel clubs.

The breed is commonly described as active, loyal, bright, playful and affectionate, and as particularly good with children. Despite its size it tends to bark to warn of strangers, making it a useful watchdog. It is first and foremost a companion that thrives on human contact.

The Japanese Spitz tolerates cold but prefers to live indoors with its family. It can live in an apartment but benefits from time running off-leash in a safe area. Mud and dirt fall or brush out of the coat easily, but the thick coat still needs brushing about twice a week to prevent knots.

The breed is described as generally healthy with few genetic problems. Conditions reported in the breed include patellar luxation, runny eyes (usually from small tear ducts or allergies) and late-onset progressive retinal atrophy of the rcd4 type. One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13 years.

faq.a: They have a thick double coat that needs regular brushing, about twice a week, though dirt does not stick to it and it is considered easy to groom.

faq.q: How long do Japanese Spitz live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13 years, slightly above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Are Japanese Spitz good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as affectionate, playful and particularly loving toward children, though any dog should be supervised around young children.
